arjun: Heads up — deploy from main (merge r4823) caused a p95 decode slowdown on our 4xA10 pool. Seen ~45ms -> ~160ms on small chat workloads. Repro locally with the same docker image we use in CI.

kevin: ugh. any obvious diff in the perf tests? CI graphs?

arjun: perf-ci shows a jump starting at the merge. The noisy test is `serve/decode/p95_short_seq`. Linking flame graph: https://perf.internal/redwood/graphs/1862/merge-r4823. Looks like attention kernels swapped to `attn_v2_fused` in some paths and we are seeing kernel selection thrash.

mia: did the merge change batching heuristics or KV eviction thresholds? those can affect how many tokens are batched and thus which kernel path is chosen.

arjun: yes — r4823 added a heuristic to prefer smaller batch sizes when prefix cache invalidation rate > 0.15 to reduce OOMs. That sounds like it could reduce effective batch size and push us to a slower kernel.

sam: can we confirm batch size distribution before/after? I ran a quick samp on canary: 
```
before: median batch=8, p90=12
after: median batch=2, p90=4
```
This matches the hypothesis.

kevin: thanks. if batch dropped to 2 then kernel selection may pick a non-fused attention that's optimized for tiny batch but has higher per-token overhead for longer tails.

perf-bot: CI perf alert: test `serve/decode/p95_short_seq` failed threshold. Baseline 50ms, current 160ms (+220%). Build: main@r4823. See run: https://ci.redwood/1862/failed

arjun: bisect started, CC @kevin @mia. Quick plan: 1) reproduce minimal repro 2) run `--kernel-selector=trace` to log chosen kernels 3) try toggling the new heuristic flag `--prefer-small-batches-on-evict` off 4) consider hotfix revert if clear.

mia: I ran `--kernel-selector=trace` on the same workload. Snip of kernel log: 
```
2026-02-14T14:12:03Z INFO kernel_select: seq_len=128 batch=2 -> chosen=attn_unfused_col32
2026-02-14T14:12:04Z INFO kernel_select: seq_len=128 batch=8 -> chosen=attn_v2_fused
```
So at batch=2 we pick `attn_unfused_col32` which is slower overall.

sam: can we force the runtime to prefer fused kernels even for small batches while we find a better heuristic? maybe a flag like `--prefer-fused=true`?

arjun: runtime already has `prefer_fused=true` but the heuristic short-circuits it when eviction_rate > threshold. So turning off the eviction gating should restore prior behavior.

kevin: quick mitigation: roll back the heuristic in Dedicated config and push a patch to main that gates the change behind a feature flag (disabled by default). That avoids a full revert.

mia: i tested locally by disabling the eviction gating: p95 drops back to ~48ms. Patch diff: 
```
- if (evict_rate > 0.15) prefer_small_batches = true;
+ if (feature_flags.enable_eviction_batching && evict_rate > 0.15) prefer_small_batches = true;
```

ci-bot: Deploy job started for candidate hotpatch branch `hotfix/evict-flag`. Build 1862145701. Tests: light perf-run queued.

perf-bot: Quick run (canary infra) shows p95 ~52ms after hotpatch on same workload.

sam: good. we should still root cause why eviction_rate jumped after merge. maybe a change to KV lifetime or cache invalidation logic?

arjun: r4823 adjusted KV cache invalidation to aggressively evict entries when we detect mismatched prefix shapes (to avoid corrupted cache entries). That increased eviction churn for certain chat patterns.

kevin: ok two threads: 1) restore perf with flag and hotpatch 2) rework invalidation to reduce churn or decouple from batching heuristic. We should also add a unit test to simulate prefix-shape churn and ensure eviction_rate stays stable.

mia: opened PR 4890 with the flag gating and a test that simulates streaming prefix churn. Marking as rollback-safe.

arjun: thanks. I'm patching production Dedicated pool configs to disable the heuristic immediately. Will monitor p95.

kevin: please file a postmortem note with numbers: baseline p95, regression p95, before/after batch distributions, and kernel mapping. Add links to flame graphs.

arjun: will do. Quick note in incidents channel and pinging infra to watch for any OOM risk since we are loosening eviction aggressiveness.

sam: reminder: add a small CI perf test that also runs with `batch=2` distribution so we detect kernel regressions that only appear at small batches.

arjun: added to the perf matrix item.

kevin: ack. great triage — thanks team :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Resolved: regression mitigated on canary pools. Follow-up: PR 4890 under review.
